$comment: This repository runs the harness on itself. Every check it offers is enforced here, because a standard whose own repository does not meet it is a suggestion.

tracks.$comment: Spec 0009. Three weeks: long enough that a lane paused over a holiday is not nagged, short enough that an abandoned one does not keep its fence for a quarter.

cleanExit.$comment: console.log is deliberately not a marker here: this is a command-line tool and its output is the product. A project picks the markers that mean 'unfinished' in its own code.

boundaries.$comment: Spec 0010. CONSTRAINTS #1 says this package never takes a runtime dependency, and until now that was a sentence a reviewer had to remember. An import in src/ that is neither a node: builtin nor relative is exactly that dependency, so the rule is now a line that fails.

rules.reason:
a runtime dependency — CONSTRAINTS #1: this package installs nothing, so `npx harnessimo` is one download and a supply chain of one
      fix:  use a node: builtin, or write the twenty lines

release.$comment: This repository published three versions to npm through a manual workflow run while its own tags stopped at v0.4.1. The check exists because of that, and it is on here first.

tokens.$comment: Spec 0004. On here because this repository is held to its own rules, and because a guard nobody runs against real work is a guard nobody has tested. The state is per-session and gitignored: it describes one run, not the repository.

autonomy.$comment: Spec 0007. Deliberately the lowest level: work here happens with someone reading each step, and `check` runs at the end of every turn through the Stop hook — a floor that re-verified the whole queue would make that gate slow enough to be removed, which is the failure mode the pre-commit hook is already shaped around. CI raises it to `unattended`, which is what CI honestly is.
